jobs.jobDescription:
Are you a BCBA passionate about early intervention and looking for the flexibility of remote work without giving up clinical impact?

At Life Skill Autism Academy, a division of Centria Autism, our Telehealth BCBAs lead center-based ABA therapy services virtually for children ages 12 and under. Our mission is clear: deliver compassionate, evidence-based care during the most critical developmental window, so every child has the best chance to thrive.

Compensation and Incentives:

Let's Talk! We know that outstanding clinical quality is invaluable, and we are ready to compensate accordingly. We invite all applicants to share their salary expectations, and we are fully prepared to tailor a package that reflects your unique clinical experience and value.

This position offers:

  1. Base salary $85,000 - $95,000 (negotiable based on experience).
  2. Monthly and weekly bonus structure averaging $1,000 or more per month!

What Centria Offers:

  • Early Intervention, Big Impact – Help shape a child’s future during the years when ABA therapy can make the most significant developmental difference.
  • Purpose-Built Centers – Our LSAA centers are thoughtfully designed for children 5 and under, with low-distraction spaces, play-based learning areas, and a strong emphasis on routines and safety.

  • Clinical Quality First – We prioritize outcomes, not billables. Our proprietary CareConnect platform streamlines everything from treatment planning to data collection so you can stay focused on care, not paperwork.
  • Assent-Based and Play-Focused – We blend Practical Functional Assessment and Skills-Based Treatment into a compassionate, assent-based model, centered around joyful, meaningful learning.
  • Real Work-Life Balance – Small caseloads, manageable schedules, and dedicated support teams mean no last-minute chaos and no burnout.
  • You're Never Alone – With layered support from Clinical Directors, Area Clinical Directors, and our Clinical Excellence Team, you'll always have someone in your corner.
  • No Operational Headaches – We handle the logistics. From scheduling to onboarding of technicians, our operations team keeps everything running smoothly behind the scenes.
  • Career Growth on Your Terms – Whether you're mentoring the next generation of BCBAs, leading clinical training, or stepping into leadership, we support your growth.
  • We Invest in You – From CEU stipends and paid CEU days to exclusive internal training events, we’re serious about keeping you sharp—and helping you level up.
  • Perks That Actually Matter – Annual, all-inclusive vacation for two, early wage access, a company car or mileage reimbursement, and full benefits.
  • No Non-Compete – We don’t believe in holding people back. If we’re not the right long-term fit, you’ll still leave better prepared for your next step.

Your Role & Impact as a BCBA

  • Lead ABA therapy delivery within a collaborative, in-center environment
  • Provide daily support and guidance to Behavior Technicians to ensure clinical excellence
  • Develop and implement assent-based, individualized behavior plans following ABA principles
  • Engage parents during scheduled on-site training sessions to drive meaningful progress
  • Maintain high-quality clinical services through regular supervision and data-driven decision-making

At Life Skills Autism Academy, you’re not just supporting kids—you’re shaping futures. Join a team that believes in early intervention, compassionate care, and your potential as a leader. Apply today and help build the foundation for a child’s lifelong success.

Centria is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or protected veteran status.

jobs.jobDescription:
At Dscout, we’re building the most flexible and powerful UX research platform on the market—trusted by the world’s top brands in finance (JP Morgan Chase, Intuit, Charles Schwab, PayPal), healthcare (Aya, Headspace), consumer goods (Keen, Verizon, Target, Northface), and tech (Google, Amazon, Facebook, Meta, Spotify, AirBnB). Our tools help teams deeply understand the humans behind their products, so they can build better ones. We are expanding our smart and driven team and would love for you to join us.

At Dscout, we're building the human-grounded layer that teaches AI to work in the real world and proves it stays aligned there. We are expanding our smart and driven team and would love for you to join us.

Dscout AI Training & Evals builds human data and evals that show whether AI works for real people. For ten years Dscout has captured how people behave in real context, with consent and scientific rigor. Dscout AI Training & Evals points that engine at AI: consented human behavior and judgment, turned into the training data, evals, and benchmarks AI teams trust.

Models ace benchmarks and still surprise people in the wild. A benchmark says how capable a model is. It does not say whether the model works for the person using it, across weeks, in the mess of real life. That gap is where we work.

We serve AI researchers, the product builders who ship alongside them, and the research teams who partner with both. We are a new unit inside an established company: live customers, a mature platform (React, Elixir, Python, Swift, Kotlin; SOC 2 and HITRUST certified), a small senior team, and room to build. We work AI-native. Agents write code, evals gate changes, and we aim to do in months what used to take years.

A note from our Chief AI Officer & GM. The hardest AI problems show up when a model meets real people, with their tools, their interruptions, and their goals. Our customers need a partner who can design the answer, build it, and ship it fast. Ground Truth sits where deployment meets research: what we learn in the field shapes the science, and the science shapes what we ship. Come build it with us.

Why this seat

  • Work directly with AI labs and AI product teams on problems that have no playbook yet.
  • Build on a platform that already works, so your time goes into the hard part, not the plumbing.
  • Own technical decisions on your programs, and see your builds become a product.
  • Join a small senior team with direct access to the GM, our Principal Engineers, and the Head of AI Research.

Our Strategic Project Leads run customer programs from first scoping call to final data delivery. You are their technical partner and builder. Customers ask for things that have not been built before: weeks of real-world AI use, captured in context, delivered as data a lab can train or evaluate on. You work out how. Some of it our platform already does, some needs configuring, and some has to be built. Knowing which is the job.

Programs you will work on

  • Long-horizon, real-world use of AI products, captured over days and weeks.
  • Side-by-side model comparisons judged by people who match a specific profile.
  • Human judgment and preference data, delivered in formats a training pipeline can ingest.
  • Feedback loops that connect real user behavior to model and product decisions.

What you will do

Scope and shape programs

  • Turn a fuzzy customer brief into a technical plan in days, alongside the Project Lead.
  • Decide what to reuse, extend, or build, and prove the gap before you write code.
  • Write the scope down: what we will deliver, how it works, what could go wrong.

Build and ship

  • Build capture flows, task logic, data pipelines, and delivery across web, mobile, and backend.
  • Ship production code with real participants on the other end.
  • Use coding agents and evals as part of how you build, and teach the habit to others.

Build trust into the data

  • Own redaction, validation, provenance, and clean delivery.
  • Design quality checks and human-review paths, and measure whether they work.
  • Work with our research team so the data you ship carries evidence that it is good.

Turn the field into product

  • Work with core engineering to move repeat builds into the platform.
  • Tell us what customers keep asking for, and help decide what we build next.

Latitude. These areas are the core, not the whole list. You will have real room to propose new program types and platform capabilities as the market moves.

A good first year

  • Several customer programs scoped and shipped, with you named by the customer.
  • Signed scope to first data gets noticeably faster.
  • Two or more custom builds absorbed into the core platform.
  • Project Leads stop asking "can we do this?" and start asking "how fast?"

How we will hire: a conversation with the GM; a scoping exercise on a real, anonymized brief (what would you reuse, what would you build); a technical deep dive with core engineers; a conversation with the Project Leads and the Head of AI Research.

What you bring

  • 7+ years shipping production full-stack software. We care more about what you have shipped than which languages you list.
  • Experience working directly with technical customers, as a forward deployed engineer, solutions engineer, or early founding engineer.
  • Experience building and running data pipelines: ingest, clean, redact, deliver.
  • Hands-on time with AI coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex or similar). You have shipped serious work with them, not just used autocomplete.
  • Experience building with LLMs and a sense of how they get evaluated. You are at ease with non-determinism and reason about behavior across a distribution, not a fixed test suite.
  • You write clearly and can explain a tradeoff to a researcher and to a PM.
  • Based in the Bay Area, with occasional customer travel.

Nice to have: human data, labeling, or eval pipeline experience; mobile or browser-based capture; sensitive or regulated data; you have founded something.

Compensation: $250-400K OTE + Equity. Includes a built-in bonus and equity program, flexible PTO, 15 holidays, 12 weeks of paid parental leave, 401k match, and an education stipend.

This is an ideal list. If the role excites you and you do not check every box, we would still love to hear from you.

Of course, what is outlined above is an ideal set of expectations; however, business needs and other projects and tasks may shift, and additional tasks could be assigned at the discretion of your manager.

About Dscout

Dscout is a team of passionate, empathetic, and curious professionals. As a recognized leader in the Forrester Wave, we’re at the cutting edge of experience research technology. The power of research drives us - how in-context insights from real people can build more enjoyable products and services.

We prioritize learning, sharing, and building. We also deeply value being a diverse and inclusive team and company and look for team members who align with that belief. Join our dynamic team and help shape product roadmaps and business strategies for the world’s most loved brands.

It doesn't stop there. When you join the Dscout team, you will get:

  • A strong and competitive compensation package with a built-in bonus and equity program.
  • An incredible and progressive benefits package (for both you and your dependents) to support work/life balance, including flexible PTO, 15 company holidays, 12 weeks of paid parental leave, 401k match, and much more.

We do not discriminate based on identity, including race, color, religion, national origin or ancestry, sex, gender identity and expression, age, physical or mental disability, pregnancy, veteran or military status, unfavorable discharge from military service, genetic information, sexual orientation, marital status, order of protection status, citizenship status, arrest record or expunged or sealed convictions, or any other legally recognized protected basis under federal, state, or local law.

Please note that only inquiries regarding requests for reasonable accommodation will be responded to from this email address.

For more information about our privacy practices, please visit our Privacy Policy.

jobs.jobDescription:
CodePath is the largest educator of college computer science students in the country. We've trained over 50,000 students from more than 1,000 universities. Our partners include Amazon, Google, and other leading technology companies. After nearly a decade of training technical talent, we launched a $150M initiative with Anthropic to prepare people for careers in AI.

We're expanding into new markets and growing our team as AI changes the workforce. People joining CodePath now will help shape this next stage of our work.

We believe technical skills create opportunities. Our goal is to train millions of learners and create lasting economic impact. If you want to build something new, take ownership, and see the results of your work, this is a place to do it.

About the Role

Location: Remote, United States

Role-Type: Full-Time, W2 Employee

Reports To: AI Practice Lead, Claude Corps

Compensation: $110,000 to $124,500 per year

Start Date: No later than February 8th, ahead of the March 8th cohort launch

Together with Anthropic, CodePath launched Claude Corps in June 2026, a national fellowship program with a $150 million commitment to place 1,000 AI-trained fellows at nonprofits across America.

As a CodePath Mentor, you are the full-time coach and guide for a portfolio of roughly ten pods: about 20 fellows across 8–12 host organizations, from pre-Basecamp through the final day of the program. Your job is to help each fellow succeed not only in building with AI, but in navigating the organization around the work: understanding the problem, identifying the right stakeholders, communicating ideas clearly, building buy-in, and turning an AI-enabled solution into something people will actually use.

The host organization directs the fellow's day-to-day work, the curriculum team owns what they learn, and your Sr. Manager of AI Practice is the manager of record who holds the performance bar. You carry the throughline across the fellow experience: you know your pods end to end, spot patterns and roadblocks early, coach fellows through ambiguity, and bring in deeper technical expertise when needed.

The work combines asynchronous coaching and feedback with regular 1:1s, office hours, milestone reviews, roadmap and project feedback, and synchronous coaching when a fellow needs more than text. Fellows may be building technical integrations, designing AI-enabled workflows, educating an organization on AI, or helping a nonprofit adopt an entirely new way of working.

You do not need to be the deepest software engineer in the room. You do need enough technical fluency to understand what fellows are building, learn unfamiliar technologies quickly, and help them reason through AI-enabled solutions. Just as importantly, you need the judgment and coaching ability to help an early-career fellow navigate the people, communication, and organizational challenges that determine whether their work succeeds.

This role is built for someone who gets energy from helping other people succeed. You may come from engineering, consulting, implementation, technical program management, AI enablement, education, or another client-facing technical environment. What matters most is that you have personally navigated ambiguity, helped people or organizations adopt technology, and can coach fellows through doing the same.

Key Responsibilities

Coach your pods

  • Carry roughly 20 pods (up to 40 fellows across 16 to 24 host organizations) full-time from pre-Basecamp through final day, calibrating your time across the portfolio rather than sinking into one pod
  • Facilitate weekly 1:1s with all Fellows who report to you and document their progress, challenges, and successes using the tooling Claude Corps operates on
  • Coach fellows through ambiguous projects, helping them clarify the problem, understand organizational context, identify stakeholders, and determine the right next step
  • Give structured feedback on fellows' real work, including project plans, roadmap drafts, architecture proposals, presentations, technical implementations, and QBR deliverables
  • Help fellows strengthen the professional skills required to succeed inside their host organizations, including communication, stakeholder management, presentations, prioritization, and navigating feedback
  • Lead each fellow's Day 30/90/180/270 milestone review; own the fellow-level synthesis and hand it up to your Sr. Manager of AI Practice, who owns the roll-up and performance call

Deliver the curriculum in your pods

  • Deliver the just-in-time modules the curriculum team designs; author lane- or pod-specific content when they commission it because you have seen the gap from closer in
  • Coach fellows on applying AI tools and workflows to real organizational problems rather than simply completing technical exercises
  • Frame and debrief the cohort-wide all-hands your Sr. Manager of AI Practice runs, and the sessions where the curriculum team or a guest teaches your fellows directly
  • Co-lead the Basecamp practical assessment alongside Anthropic's instructors; it is your first calibration on each cohort

Help fellows navigate organizations

  • Coach fellows through stakeholder discovery, requirements gathering, presentations, organizational buy-in, and change management
  • Help fellows translate between technical possibilities and the business or mission needs of their host organizations
  • Guide fellows through situations where the technical solution is only part of the challenge and adoption, communication, or organizational alignment is the real blocker
  • Model how to work effectively with technical and nontechnical stakeholders, particularly in organizations that may be early in their AI adoption journey

Keep the program honest

  • When the same problem shows up across three fellows, raise it to the right owner: the Claude Corps leadership team for program efficacy, the curriculum team for curriculum, partner experts for technical depth, host-org managers for a host issue, or your Sr. Manager of AI Practice for a delivery or performance issue
  • Be the first stop when a fellow's work is at risk, whether the roadblock is technical, organizational, or professional; surface significant risks to your Sr. Manager of AI Practice, who owns the escalation
  • Work AI-natively: Claude and other modern AI tools should be core to how you research, build, coach, problem-solve, identify patterns, and provide feedback at scale
  • Help fellows develop the judgment to use AI effectively, not simply the ability to operate a particular tool

Key Success Metrics

  • Fellows can point to concrete examples of how your coaching improved their technical judgment, communication, or ability to navigate their host organization
  • 100% of host-org managers you've worked with in the last 30 days can produce one concrete example of your impact
  • You consistently identify recurring technical, professional, and organizational patterns across your pods and surface them to the right program owner
  • Every Day 30 review is done and documented, handed up to your Sr. Manager of AI Practice, with a plan for any fellow whose work is at risk or ready for the next challenge

Qualifications

Required

  • 2–5 years of previous professional experience in software engineering, IT, data, technical program management, implementation, solutions engineering, forward deployed engineering, technical consulting, AI operations, or another technically adjacent role
  • Hands-on, current experience using modern AI tools and workflows. You should be able to speak concretely about how you use tools such as Claude, AI agents, LLM-based applications, automation, or similar technologies to solve real problems
  • Real coaching, mentorship, people-development, or management experience with concrete examples of helping someone navigate a challenge and become more successful
  • Experience working across stakeholders to understand a problem, clarify needs, recommend or implement a solution, and help people adopt a new way of working
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills, including the ability to facilitate discussions, coach someone through an important presentation, and provide thoughtful asynchronous feedback
  • Comfortable operating as a technical generalist: you can learn quickly, ask the right questions, understand unfamiliar systems, and bring in deeper expertise when needed
  • Comfortable coaching early-career professionals through ambiguity, feedback, organizational dynamics, and the expectations of working in a professional environment
  • Comfortable with remote, synchronous obligations across U.S. time zones and about two evenings a month for cohort sessions and milestone reviews

Preferred

  • Client-facing consulting or implementation experience, particularly working with small businesses, nonprofits, education organizations, or teams adopting new technology

Full-Time Employee Benefits

  • Financial Security: 401(k), employer-paid life & disability insurance, and identity theft protection
  • Work-Life Balance: Generous PTO, paid holidays, 10 weeks of fully paid parental leave, and an annual year-end company closure (Dec 24 – Jan 2)

jobs.jobDescription:
ABOUT QUINCE

Quince is a destination for builders, creators, innovators, and operators who want to come together and challenge the status quo. Our mission is simple: make really high quality essentials for really low prices, fairly and sustainably. We deliver on that mission through a unique manufacturer-to-consumer (M2C) model eliminating the layers of traditional retail that add cost and result in consumers paying more than they need to. We find, build relationships with, and work directly with the manufacturing partners behind some of the world’s finest products. From there, our teams design smart, efficient operational processes and build and deploy proprietary technology, AI, and analytics to help us scale fast.

What began with a small assortment of elevated basics has quickly grown into a cross-category brand spanning apparel, accessories, home goods, and more. Today, tens of millions of people across a growing number of countries come – and return – to Quince because they trust us to deliver.

OUR CULTURE

Quince is a culture built for builders by builders. Our way of working starts with a blank sheet of paper. We question conventional thinking, use technology and data to uncover new opportunities, and move quickly to turn ideas into reality. We aren’t interested in replicating how others do retail. We’re building a better way – at a speed and scale unlike anything that’s been done before.

  • We dream big and chase the hard problems others shy away from. Rejecting long-held assumptions is part of our company's DNA. Where conventional wisdom says you have to choose – soft or durable, speed or rigor, quality or price – we ask why that trade-off has to exist in the first place.
  • Our pace is fast and the bar is high because our customers expect a lot from us and we refuse to let them down. We believe the best results come from challenging ourselves, learning from one another, and building on each other's strengths.
  • Here, responsibility is not determined by role, tenure, or seniority. Every team member - no matter their level - has the opportunity to drive our business and shape our trajectory.

If you’re someone who likes to imagine new possibilities and build better systems rather than plug-in to outdated ones, Quince is the place for you.

THE ROLE

Recruiting Systems Administrator

We are looking for a Recruiting Systems Administrator to own the day-to-day administration and optimization of our talent acquisition tech stack. You will be the go-to expert for Greenhouse (ATS), ModernLoop (interview scheduling) and adjacent recruiting tools, including systems built in-house. You will keep these systems configured, connected, and running cleanly so recruiters and coordinators can move fast and hiring teams have a seamless experience. You will also help shape and maintain the talent tooling we build in-house. This is a hands-on role for someone who loves solving problems, tightening processes, and finding opportunities to automate repetitive work as we scale hiring across the business.

Responsibilities

  • Administer and configure Greenhouse, ModernLoop, and adjacent recruiting tools, including job templates, interview plans, scorecards, approval chains, and permissions.
  • Manage user access, roles, and permission groups across the TA stack, ensuring the right people have the right level of access and offboarding is timely.
  • Build and maintain recruiting workflows and automations that reduce manual steps for recruiters and coordinators.
  • Own data hygiene in the ATS, including deduplication, field standardization, and routine audits to keep reporting reliable.
  • Support integrations between recruiting tools and downstream systems, and partner with the Systems Engineers on troubleshooting data feeds.
  • Serve as tier-one support for recruiter and coordinator system questions, triaging issues and resolving them or escalating with clear context.
  • Coordinate with vendors on support tickets, release management, new feature rollouts, and configuration changes.
  • Document system configurations, standard operating procedures, and training materials so knowledge does not live in one person's head.
  • Identify and implement opportunities to automate recruiting operations, applying AI-enabled tooling to improve speed and accuracy.

Qualifications

  • 5+ years of experience administering recruiting or HR systems, with hands-on Greenhouse or comparable ATS administration.
  • Strong working knowledge of interview scheduling tools such as ModernLoop and their configuration.
  • Demonstrated experience managing user access, permissions, and workflow configuration in SaaS platforms.
  • A track record of improving data hygiene and building reporting-ready processes.
  • Experience supporting integrations between systems and coordinating with vendors on troubleshooting.
  • An automation mindset and comfort using AI-enabled tools to streamline repetitive operational work.
  • Excellent problem-solving skills and strong attention to detail, with the ability to translate recruiter needs into system solutions.
  • Clear written communication and a habit of documenting processes for a scaling team.
  • Experience with SQL and APIs a plus

All posted ranges are reflective of base salary and may vary depending upon experience level and location. Bonus and equity may also be provided for eligible roles.

Pay Range

$126,000—$172,000 USD

WHY QUINCE?

Joining Quince means being part of a mission-driven team reshaping retail. You will work alongside talented colleagues, tackle meaningful challenges, and contribute to building a more sustainable, accessible future for customers and partners alike.

EQUAL OPPORTUNITY & HIRING INTEGRITY

Quince provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applications for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran or military status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws.

Quince is committed to providing reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with disabilities. If you need a reasonable accommodation to complete your application or to perform the essential functions of a role at Quince, please let us know by completing this accommodation form. We review all requests individually and will work with you to determine appropriate accommodations on a case-by-case basis.

Employment is contingent upon successful completion of a background check. Quince will conduct background checks in compliance with applicable federal, state, and local laws.

Security Advisory: Beware of Frauds

At Quince, we're dedicated to recruiting top talent who share our drive for innovation. To safeguard candidates, Quince emphasizes legitimate recruitment practices. Initial communication is primarily via official Quince email addresses and LinkedIn; beware of deviations. Personal data and sensitive information will not be solicited during the application phase. Interviews are conducted via phone, in person, or through the approved platforms Google Meets or Zoom—never via messaging apps or other calling services. Offers are merit-based, communicated verbally, and followed up in writing. If personal information is requested to initiate the hiring process, rest assured it will be through secure and protected means.

jobs.jobDescription:
Tremendous is the global platform built for businesses to send thousands of payouts to anyone, anywhere, for free. We're trusted by 20,000 organizations like Atlassian, MIT, and United Way to deliver gift cards and money to millions of recipients worldwide.

Our customers (researchers, marketers, HR teams, nonprofits, and platform businesses) rave about how fast and easy Tremendous is to use. Check out our ratings on G2.

Tremendous is profitable and growing without outside investors. We’re a fully remote, high-documentation, low-meeting culture, which means more time for what matters in both your professional and personal life. The team agrees– our employee NPS is in the high 80s.

Design at Tremendous

We design experiences that make complex systems feel straightforward and intuitive by taking our time to get things right. We favor depth and scale over speed, while raising the bar for quality so our product stays ahead of the competition. We’re a place for designers who care about doing things well.

About the role

We're hiring a Senior Product Designer to raise the craft of the product across Tremendous.

You'll report to our Director of Product Design and work horizontally. Craft projects across the dashboard and the recipient experience: navigation, information architecture, the design system, motion. You'll also take small projects from pods that have no designer. Those teams have little user experience work of their own, which is why this is a Foundations role.

What you'll do

  • Raise the craft of the product. Dashboard and recipient experience. Navigation, information architecture, how things open and close, empty states. Motion, micro-interactions, and transitions are a big part of the job.

  • Own the design system, and raise it. Set patterns other designers can follow with clear documentation. Close gaps that produce one-off UI. Push the quality of the system itself.

  • Set a vision for product foundations. Where craft, UX, and UI should go so the product holds up next to Stripe or Brex. Make that vision concrete enough to build toward.

  • Cover work that has no designer. Small projects from pods without an embedded designer.

  • Partner with an engineer. You'll work with an engineer focused on shipping this craft work with you. Use AI to prototype, show how something should feel, and help engineering implement it.

  • Designers at Tremendous own the copy in their designs.

What you'll bring

  • 8+ years as a product designer, including experience working on B2B products. You can do the product thinking: edge cases, shipping work that has to hold up in a real product.

  • High craft. Strong visual design, UI, and motion. Your portfolio shows it.

  • You've owned and improved a design system.

  • You've done information architecture and set a product vision or redesign. You can tell that story.

  • Strong communication and storytelling, written and verbal.

  • You use AI in your design work, including prototyping (v0, Claude, Cursor, or similar).

What's cool about the role

  • Ship work you’ll be proud of.

  • Competitive pay and equity. Base salary for this role: $200,000 - $265,000.

  • Real benefits. 100% covered health (US), unlimited PTO, 12-16 weeks paid parental leave.

  • Fully remote. Work from anywhere in the Americas.

  • Great culture. Read more about how we work in our public handbook.

jobs.jobDescription:
At Dscout, we’re building the most flexible and powerful UX research platform on the market—trusted by the world’s top brands in finance (JP Morgan Chase, Intuit, Charles Schwab, PayPal), healthcare (Aya, Headspace), consumer goods (Keen, Verizon, Target, Northface), and tech (Google, Amazon, Facebook, Meta, Spotify, AirBnB). Our tools help teams deeply understand the humans behind their products, so they can build better ones. We are expanding our smart and driven team and would love for you to join us.

As a recognized leader in the Forrester Wave, we’re at the cutting edge of experience research technology. Join our dynamic team and work with advanced AI and research tools to analyze data, recruit diverse participants, and deliver insights that shape product roadmaps and business strategies. As a fast-growing, Series C-funded company, we offer you the chance to make a real impact in the user experience field while advancing your career.

We are looking for a Customer Research Advisor to join our growing Customer Experience and Research (CXR) team. YOU MUST RESIDE IN CHICAGO, AUSTIN OR SAN FRANCISCO! In this position, you will work collaboratively with Lead Research Advisors and Dscout clients to help our customers use our platform to design, recruit and field research projects. Our clients conduct research on a wide range of topics across: technology, retail, healthcare, and AI, just to name a few. You will have a chance to make a real difference for Dscout’s customers and build your career in the worlds of research and customer success.

You are an incredible communicator and a genuine, creative problem-solver. You’re the client’s partner in learning a new digital tool to execute powerful research. You collaborate with clients as they develop research plans and help to identify Dscout methodologies that best meet their needs. Internally, you are our clients’ champion to drive larger improvements to the platform and overall user experience. The Research Advisor position is among the most central to dscout’s operations and means you’ll work with people from across the company on a regular basis, especially our product, engineering and sales teams. If this sounds exciting to you, apply today! Salary range is 75-80K

What You Will Do:

  • Act as a true Dscout expert to train and educate clients on features and functionalities
  • Provide specific recommendations for clients’ research design on Dscout
  • Assist in running clients’ research projects on Dscout including planning, designing, recruiting, fielding, analysis, and client engagement
  • Assist in the creation of training and educational materialsAssist with billing and other administrative processes for clients
  • Provide support and guidance to research participants to ensure the information they share is helpful and that they enjoy participating
  • Act as a customer advocate by sharing client feedback internally to continuously improve Dscout’s product offerings

What you Need to Have:

  • BA/BS in design research, psychology, anthropology, sociology, market research, or a related field (or equivalent work experience); MA/MS in these areas is also nice to have, but not required
  • 1 - 4 years of professional experience (non-internship experience)
  • 2 - 4 years of client facing or similar experience
  • Strong track record with client-facing responsibilities, with experience in client service and client relationship management
  • Strong track record of interpreting clients’ needs and meeting or exceeding their expectations
  • Strong project and time management skills; able to simultaneously manage multiple projects across multiple stakeholders
  • Established knowledge of and passion for user research, UX and/or consumer researchInterest or experience in conducting qualitative analysis
  • Naturally able to strike a balance between friendly and professional in communications
  • Able to work both collaboratively and independently
  • Flexible and eager to learn new things each and every day
  • Genuinely interested in research and technology: you're technically curious, you enjoy learning about new products, and you are fascinated about how things work
  • Curious and empathetic to others’ needs and circumstances
  • Highly organized, efficient and detail-oriented

Of course, what is outlined above is an ideal set of expectations; however, business needs and other projects and tasks may shift, and additional tasks could be assigned at the discretion of your manager.

About Dscout

Dscout is a team of passionate, empathetic, and curious professionals. As a recognized leader in the Forrester Wave, we’re at the cutting edge of experience research technology. The power of research drives us - how in-context insights from real people can build more enjoyable products and services.

We prioritize learning, sharing, and building. We also deeply value being a diverse and inclusive team and company and look for team members who align with that belief. Join our dynamic team and help shape product roadmaps and business strategies for the world’s most loved brands.

It doesn't stop there. When you join the Dscout team, you will get:

  • A strong and competitive compensation package with a built-in bonus and equity program.
  • An incredible and progressive benefits package (for both you and your dependents) to support work/life balance, including flexible PTO, 15 company holidays, 12 weeks of paid parental leave, 401k match, and much more.
  • An education stipend to support your growth & development, and a remote work stipend.
  • A company that is open and transparent with our team. You will know what is happening and why it matters.

Dscout is an equal-opportunity employer that values diversity. We do not discriminate based on identity, including race, color, religion, national origin or ancestry, sex, gender identity and expression, age, physical or mental disability, pregnancy, veteran or military status, unfavorable discharge from military service, genetic information, sexual orientation, marital status, order of protection status, citizenship status, arrest record or expunged or sealed convictions, or any other legally recognized protected basis under federal, state, or local law.

If you need reasonable accommodations for any part of the employment process, please email us at accommodations@dscout.com with the nature of your request and your contact information. We'll do everything possible to ensure you're well-prepared for success during our interview process, while also upholding your privacy, including accommodating any special requests. Please note that only inquiries regarding requests for reasonable accommodation will be responded to from this email address.

When you apply at Dscout, we will process your job applicant data, including your employment and education history, transcript, writing samples, and references, as necessary to consider your job application for open positions. For more information about our privacy practices, please visit our Privacy Policy.

Dscout participates in the E-Verify program in certain locations, as required by law.

Location Flexibility: Dscout is proud to support a remote-first workforce and enable employees to work from almost anywhere. At this time, however, we are unable to hire in the following locations: Montana, Hawaii, Alaska, and Washington DC.

NOTE: DSCOUT NEVER CONTACTS JOB APPLICANTS VIA TEXT, MESSENGER, OR OTHER SIMILAR APPLICATIONS. BE AWARE OF PHISHING AND SPOOFING SCAMS, BOTH VIA TEXT AND EMAIL. ONLY RESPOND TO EMAILS FROM DSCOUT.COM

jobs.jobDescription:
CodePath is the largest educator of college computer science students in the country. We've trained over 50,000 students from more than 1,000 universities. Our partners include Amazon, Google, and other leading technology companies. After nearly a decade of training technical talent, we launched a $150M initiative with Anthropic to prepare people for careers in AI.

We're expanding into new markets and growing our team as AI changes the workforce. People joining CodePath now will help shape this next stage of our work.

We believe technical skills create opportunities. Our goal is to train millions of learners and create lasting economic impact. If you want to build something new, take ownership, and see the results of your work, this is a place to do it.

About the Role

Location: Remote (US)

Role Type: Full-Time Contractor (40 hours/week)

Duration: 9-month contract

Reports To: Sr. Manager, Development Operations

Compensation: $7,000–9,200 per month

This is not a traditional nonprofit grant writing role.

CodePath's Philanthropy Partnerships team raises the capital behind our courses, our career support, and our students' outcomes. The Grant Writer is how that case gets made. You write for national foundations and corporate partners deciding where their social impact dollars go, and you translate program data, student outcomes, and organizational strategy into the proposals and reports that win major commitments and steward them.

The second half of the job makes the first half repeatable. You partner with Finance, Delivery, Higher Education, and Data to stay ahead of fast-moving program updates and impact metrics, then turn what you learn into reusable assets, writing frameworks, and AI-enabled workflows the whole team draws on.

CodePath is an AI-native organization, and we expect this role to work like one. Writing faster with AI is table stakes. We want someone who builds the systems that raise everyone's output — so the team spends its time on strategy and judgment instead of rebuilding the same narrative from scratch.

CodePath is scaling fast. This is the role that lets our fundraising capacity scale with it.

Key Activities

Proposal development (~20%)

  • Lead or support major grant proposals, concepts, and letters of inquiry from prospecting through submission, meeting every funder guideline and submission requirement
  • Translate CodePath's mission, programs, and impact into compelling, consistent narratives the whole team can use
  • Research, synthesize, and translate program data into funder-facing briefs, proposals, and supporting materials
  • Build the frameworks and narratives that equip account owners to lead complex, high-value opportunities

Grant reporting and compliance (~10%)

  • Serve as lead or supporting writer on major funder reports
  • Equip account owners with the narratives, data, and frameworks they need to lead complex funder reports and steward high-value relationships
  • Proactively manage funder portal accounts, submission calendars, and organizational credentials
  • Keep internal grant management systems (e.g., Asana) current

Asset development and maintenance (~20%)

  • Build and maintain a shared library of reusable narrative assets — program descriptions, boilerplate language, proof points — that accelerates every proposal the team writes
  • Support fundraisers with ad-hoc narrative development

Cross-functional collaboration (~20%)

  • In partnership with the Sr. Manager of Development Operations, collaborate with other departments (e.g., Finance, Delivery, Higher Education, and Data) to collect and translate data, program updates, and student stories into funder-facing narratives
  • Supply narrative inputs, source content, program context, data, and proof points for donor-facing assets alongside fundraisers and the rest of the Philanthropy Partnerships team

Writing enablement and team optimization (~30%)

  • Use AI tools to improve how proposals, reports, and assets get built
  • Track fast-moving organizational developments and impact metrics to keep fundraising materials current and accurate
  • Develop and maintain proposal templates, writing frameworks, reusable assets, and funder-specific approaches that let account owners lead complex proposals and reports themselves
  • Document writing patterns and organizational knowledge to improve AI-assisted drafting and automate routine work, while holding quality, accuracy, and a consistent CodePath voice

Key Success Metrics

At 30 days

  • You understand CodePath's mission, program model, core narratives, impact data, and active funder portfolio
  • You know the team's proposal and reporting workflows, writing standards, and priorities
  • You have met the cross-functional teams and know where the information you need lives

At 60 days

  • You have contributed to active proposals or reports, turning existing CodePath information into clear, accurate funder-facing writing
  • You manage your assigned deliverables and deadlines, including funder requirements
  • You have added new or updated materials to the shared asset library
  • You have working relationships with key Finance, Delivery, Higher Education, and Data counterparts

At 90 days

  • You write proposals and reports that come back with strategic refinements, not substantive rewrites
  • You run assigned deliverables independently from information gathering through submission
  • You navigate cross-functional relationships efficiently to get what you need
  • The shared library is stronger — easier for the team to find, adapt, and keep current
  • You have shipped at least two repeatable or AI-enabled workflows that cut manual effort or free the team for higher-value work
  • Account owners are leading their own proposals and reports on complex opportunities, using frameworks and synthesis you built
  • You are a trusted writing partner to the Philanthropy Partnerships team

Qualifications

Required

  • 5–7 years writing for institutional and corporate funders — proposals, letters of inquiry, and funder reports. Long-form, funder-facing, and written by you.
  • You build with AI, you don't just write with it. You have documented recurring work, streamlined it with AI tools, and handed the result to other people. Using Claude or ChatGPT to polish a draft is not what we mean.
  • You do your own data synthesis. You go to the data and finance teams, ask the right questions, and turn what you get back into accurate narrative — without waiting for someone to hand you a summary.
  • You collaborate across functions and come in curious. You want to understand the programs and the strategy, not just the ask.
  • You work at pace. Concurrent deadlines, shifting priorities, and information that changes under you.
  • Exceptional writing and editing, with attention to detail while maintaining a strategic perspective.

Preferred

  • Experience in education, workforce development, or youth-serving nonprofits
  • Experience in a social impact, tech, or tech-adjacent environment
  • CRM management, HubSpot preferred
  • Asana or similar project management platforms
  • Comfort building simple visual assets (e.g., Canva)

Pay range

$7,000—$9,200 USD

jobs.jobDescription:
Job Title: Financial Analyst (P2)

Location: Remote

THE OPPORTUNITY:

At Salesloft, our Financial Analyst will be pivotal to our company’s success. You will be a key member of our fast-growing and high-performing Finance team and will be a critical partner in scaling the company by building key business relationships across the organization. We believe that the most successful SaaS businesses rely on agile, data-driven finance partners who look beyond budget variances to turn operational data into strategic growth.

On a day-to-day basis, you will be responsible for serving as the dedicated finance partner to our Customer Success, Professional Services, and G&A organizations alongside our FP&A leadership. Specifically, you will:

  • Lead Financial Partnering: Support departmental heads with headcount management, monthly budgeting, forecasting, and actuals variance analysis.
  • Maintain Revenue & Retention Metrics: Own the source of truth for retention and churn forecasting models, partnering directly with Revenue Operations and Order Management to ensure data integrity.
  • Drive Executive Reporting: Prepare monthly and quarterly management reporting—analyzing financial results, identifying key operational trends, and communicating insights to senior leadership.
  • Leverage Modern Tech & AI: Utilize Pigment as our core FP&A planning platform and Claude AI to accelerate data analysis, reporting, and scenario modeling to automate finance workflows.
  • Execute Strategic Modeling: Perform ad-hoc financial modeling and scenario analyses to evaluate operational risks and strategic business initiatives.

In addition to working with amazing colleagues who exemplify our ‘team over self’ core value, you will also have the opportunity to work directly across different management levels to solve complex financial challenges and shape how we scale a world-class revenue platform. You will have an opportunity to make a difference.

WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR:

We are seeking a self-motivated, customer-centric, and highly analytical problem solver who is passionate about making an impact. You are an independent thinker with an eye for process improvement, comfortable navigating fast-paced environments, and eager to leverage cutting-edge tools to automate finance workflows. If you’re looking for an opportunity to learn more, do more, and become more, then becoming a Financial Analyst is the career path for you!

THE TEAM:

Our Clari + Salesloft Finance team is comprised of seasoned and up-and-coming finance and analytics professionals who are all aligned on one vision and mission:

  • Vision: Fundamentally transform the way buyers and sellers drive repeatable outcomes
  • Mission: Bring science to the art of sales

The Finance team consists of results-oriented SaaS professionals with a strong analytical mindset and a passion for strategic problem solving. The team members share a few common traits: they are collaborative, highly curious, detail-oriented, and focused on helping the company scale cleanly.

THE SKILL SET:

  • 2 to 3 years of experience in FP&A, Sales Operations, or quantitative financial analysis roles within a high-growth tech or B2B SaaS environment.
  • Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel / Google Sheets for financial modeling.
  • Hands-on experience with modern FP&A platforms (specifically Pigment) and comfort using AI tools (such as Claude AI) to drive analytical productivity.
  • Solid understanding of core SaaS post-sales business metrics (e.g., NRR, GRR, Churn, ARR).
  • Strong communication, interpersonal, and presentation skills to interact effectively with business partners and executive management.
  • High adaptability and problem-solving skills; comfortable working in a fast-paced team with evolving priorities.
  • Collaborative mentality by prioritizing ‘we’ and not focusing on ‘me’.

BENEFITS:

Your well-being matters to us. We offer a competitive, holistic benefits program designed to support your physical, mental, and financial health at every stage of your life and career. jobs.jobDescription:
ABOUT QUINCE

Quince is a destination for builders, creators, innovators, and operators who want to come together and challenge the status quo. Our mission is simple: make really high quality essentials for really low prices, fairly and sustainably. We deliver on that mission through a unique manufacturer-to-consumer (M2C) model eliminating the layers of traditional retail that add cost and result in consumers paying more than they need to. We find, build relationships with, and work directly with the manufacturing partners behind some of the world’s finest products. From there, our teams design smart, efficient operational processes and build and deploy proprietary technology, AI, and analytics to help us scale fast.

What began with a small assortment of elevated basics has quickly grown into a cross-category brand spanning apparel, accessories, home goods, and more. Today, tens of millions of people across a growing number of countries come – and return – to Quince because they trust us to deliver.

OUR CULTURE

Quince is a culture built for builders by builders. Our way of working starts with a blank sheet of paper. We question conventional thinking, use technology and data to uncover new opportunities, and move quickly to turn ideas into reality. We aren’t interested in replicating how others do retail. We’re building a better way – at a speed and scale unlike anything that’s been done before.

  • We dream big and chase the hard problems others shy away from. Rejecting long-held assumptions is part of our company's DNA. Where conventional wisdom says you have to choose – soft or durable, speed or rigor, quality or price – we ask why that trade-off has to exist in the first place.
  • Our pace is fast and the bar is high because our customers expect a lot from us and we refuse to let them down. We believe the best results come from challenging ourselves, learning from one another, and building on each other's strengths.
  • Here, responsibility is not determined by role, tenure, or seniority. Every team member - no matter their level - has the opportunity to drive our business and shape our trajectory.

If you’re someone who likes to imagine new possibilities and build better systems rather than plug-in to outdated ones, Quince is the place for you.

Quince is seeking a highly analytical, technical, and operationally minded Program Manager, Materials Planning to support material procurement and sourcing across our global manufacturing and supplier network. This role plays a critical part in ensuring alignment between sourcing strategies, production capabilities, and operational goals.

The ideal candidate brings a strong foundation in supply chain concepts, a collaborative mindset, and a desire to grow into increasing levels of ownership and impact.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Support material procurement and sourcing activities across Quince’s manufacturing and supply base
  • Partner with internal teams and external suppliers to align sourcing strategies with production capacity and operational priorities
  • Evaluate supplier performance across quality, reliability, and operational metrics; identify risks and improvement opportunities
  • Collaborate cross-functionally with Planning, Merchandising, and Sourcing teams to support execution, decision-making, and performance visibility
  • Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives that enhance planning efficiency, supplier performance, and overall value creation
  • Support reporting and analytics to inform procurement decisions and operational performance

REQUIREMENTS:

  • Foundational understanding of supply chain concepts, including procurement, inventory management, sourcing, and manufacturing operations
  • Experience or comfort working with analytics and reporting tools such as Excel, Power BI, Tableau, SQL, or similar
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
  • Ability to interpret data and translate insights into actionable recommendations

YEAR ONE DELIVERABLES

  • Material In-Stock Rate > 95%: Ensure consistent material availability to support production and minimize disruptions
  • Weeks of Supply (WOS): Maintain optimal inventory levels by balancing availability with working capital efficiency
  • Lead Time Accuracy > 90%: Improve and stabilize supplier and material lead times to support planning accuracy and responsiveness
  • Forecast Accuracy > 80%: Partner with cross-functional teams to improve demand and material forecast accuracy

All posted ranges are reflective of base salary and may vary depending upon experience level and location. Bonus and equity may also be provided for eligible roles.

Pay Range

$137,000—$185,000 USD

WHY QUINCE?

Joining Quince means being part of a mission-driven team reshaping retail. You will work alongside talented colleagues, tackle meaningful challenges, and contribute to building a more sustainable, accessible future for customers and partners alike.

EQUAL OPPORTUNITY & HIRING INTEGRITY

Quince provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applications for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran or military status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws.

Quince is committed to providing reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with disabilities. If you need a reasonable accommodation to complete your application or to perform the essential functions of a role at Quince, please let us know by completing this accommodation form. We review all requests individually and will work with you to determine appropriate accommodations on a case-by-case basis.

Employment is contingent upon successful completion of a background check. Quince will conduct background checks in compliance with applicable federal, state, and local laws.

jobs.jobDescription:
Who We Are

At OKX, we believe that the future will be reshaped by crypto, and ultimately contribute to every individual's freedom. OKX is a leading crypto exchange, and the developer of OKX Wallet, giving millions access to crypto trading and decentralized crypto applications (dApps). OKX is also a trusted brand by hundreds of large institutions seeking access to crypto markets. We are safe and reliable, backed by our Proof of Reserves. Across our multiple offices globally, we are united by our core principles: We Before Me, Do the Right Thing, and Get Things Done. These shared values drive our culture, shape our processes, and foster a friendly, rewarding, and diverse environment for every OK-er.

About the Opportunity

The Americas Compliance team is hiring a Senior Compliance Manager to own compliance for OKXICE TSV. OKXICE TSV is the tokenized securities venue run by the OKX and Intercontinental Exchange joint venture under the SEC's Innovation Exemption, and it lets eligible US users trade tokenized US-listed stocks on-chain. You'll be the main person accountable for meeting the exemption's ongoing conditions. You'll work closely with Legal, Product, Web3 Risk Control and our AML, Sanctions and Surveillance teams. This is a new role on a new type of venue, so you'll help build the program as well as run it.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Own the compliance program for the venue's SEC exemption, including tracking each condition, testing controls and keeping records ready for regulatory examination.

  • Manage the venue's public notice: review revisions, control versions, and make sure the notice matches how the product actually works. This includes corrections and material-change filings within the required deadlines.

  • Run the issuer notice process from start to finish, including tracking delivery, handling objections and confirming each stock's listing date.

  • Track and monitor TSV limits on an ongoing basis, including per-stock and volume limits against consolidated market data, periodic tier rechecks, trading halts and eligible stablecoins. Escalate breaches, significant operational events and required SEC notifications.

  • Oversee participant onboarding and ongoing wallet maintenance and monitoring, including KYC/KYB, daily sanctions and on-chain wallet rescreening, keeping wallet-to-participant records current, and issuing and revoking the soulbound token (SBT) credential that grants access.

  • Report to the OKXICE LLC Board of Managers and to Americas Compliance leadership, and manage and develop a TSV Compliance Analyst.

What We Look For In You

  • 8+ years of compliance experience at a broker-dealer, exchange, alternative trading system (ATS) or digital asset firm, with direct experience of SEC-regulated activity.

  • Working knowledge of the federal securities laws that apply to trading venues, such as Regulation ATS, Regulation NMS and market manipulation rules, plus the ability to apply them to new market structures.

  • Experience building or running compliance programs under regulatory conditions, exemptive relief or no-action positions.

  • Familiarity with how blockchain-based trading works, including self-custodied wallets, smart contracts, liquidity pools and on-chain screening.

  • Strong drafting skills, with experience turning complex technical or legal detail into clear public disclosures and procedures.

  • Sound judgment and the ability to work with Product, Engineering and Legal teams across time zones.

Nice to Haves

  • Experience with tokenized securities, transfer agents or digital asset broker-dealers.

  • Exposure to OFAC sanctions programs and blocked property handling for on-chain assets.

  • Experience reporting to a board or joint venture governance body.

  • A JD or a similar legal background.

Perks & Benefits

  • Competitive total compensation package

  • Various team building programs and company events

  • Wellness and meal allowances

  • Comprehensive healthcare schemes for employees and dependants

  • More that we love to tell you along the process!

OKX Statement:

OKX is committed to equal employment opportunities regardless of race, color, genetic information, creed, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, lawful alien status, national origin, age, marital status, and non-job related physical or mental disability, or protected veteran status. Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

Notice:

All official OKX vacancies are published on this website. While roles may appear on selected third-party platforms from time to time, information on other sites may be inaccurate or outdated. If in doubt, please apply directly through our official careers website.

Information collected and processed as part of the recruitment process of any job application you choose to submit is subject to OKX's Candidate Privacy Notice.

jobs.jobDescription:
Tremendous is the global platform built for businesses to send thousands of payouts to anyone, anywhere, for free. We're trusted by 20,000 organizations like Atlassian, MIT, and United Way to deliver gift cards and money to millions of recipients worldwide.

Our customers (researchers, marketers, HR teams, nonprofits, and platform businesses) rave about how fast and easy Tremendous is to use. Check out our ratings on G2.

Tremendous is profitable and growing without outside investors. We're a fully remote, high-documentation, low-meeting culture, which means more time for what matters in both your professional and personal life. The team agrees– our employee NPS is in the high 80s.

About the role

We're ~175 people across the US, Canada, the UK, Brazil, and elsewhere, and we're launching our first dedicated people function. You'll own people operations end to end, you'll be the person anyone at the company can go to when something is wrong, and you'll run our immigration program in conjunction with outside counsel.

What you'll do

  • Own our HRIS and associated systems

  • Administer benefits for US, Canadian, and international employees: open enrollment, carrier and broker escalations, HSA and FSA, COBRA, 401(k), and required annual notices.

  • Own the employee handbook, HR wiki, and people policies. Write the ones we're missing.

  • Own onboarding end to end: cohort logistics, new hire paperwork, and the first-90-days experience. Own offboarding, exit interviews, and severance logistics.

  • Be the company's HR point of contact. Take reports, run investigations, and write up findings. Build the intake, trust, and escalation process that makes reporting feel obvious and low-risk.

  • Run our biannual HR cycle — performance check-ins, compensation review, and the employee engagement survey — on schedule, and improve it each time.

  • Handle off-cycle compensation changes, promotions, relocations, and international moves, and the comp implications that come with them.

  • Partner with recruiting on international employment models (EOR, contractor)

  • Own our immigration program: manage active O-1, L-1A, H-1B, and PERM matters end to end, drive outside counsel on timelines, track renewals and expirations before they become urgent, and own I-9 compliance and verification.

What we're looking for

  • You have excellent judgment in situations with no precedent, and you write down your reasoning.

  • People trust you quickly, including people who don't know you yet. You hold confidences absolutely.

  • You're proactive. You'd rather build the tracker than field the emergency.

  • You're comfortable being senior and still doing the unglamorous work. This role includes open enrollment reminders and chasing I-9 signatures.

  • You write clearly. We're a documentation-first company and you'll be writing policies, investigation summaries, and company-wide comms.

What you'll bring

  • 5+ years in people operations, HR, or a people partner role, including time at a company without a large HR team

  • Experience independently running workplace investigations, including harassment matters, and writing defensible documentation

  • Deep experience administering US benefits and leave; global benefits experience is a bonus

  • Strong HRIS experience; Rippling preferred

  • Direct, hands-on experience with employment-based immigration: H-1B, O-1, L-1, and PERM

  • Experience running performance and compensation cycles for 100+ people

What's cool about the role

  • You're the first. You'll define what the people function is here rather than inheriting someone else's version of it, with direct access to leadership and real latitude to decide how this works.

  • Competitive pay and equity. Base salary for this role: $130k to $175k.

  • Real benefits. 100% covered health (US), unlimited PTO, 12-16 weeks paid parental leave.

  • Fully remote. Work from anywhere in the Americas.

  • Great culture. Read more about how we work in our public handbook.

jobs.jobDescription:
At Dscout, we’re building the most flexible and powerful UX research platform on the market—trusted by the world’s top brands in finance (JP Morgan Chase, Intuit, Charles Schwab, PayPal), healthcare (Aya, Headspace), consumer goods (Keen, Verizon, Target, Northface), and tech (Google, Amazon, Facebook, Meta, Spotify, AirBnB). Our tools help teams deeply understand the humans behind their products, so they can build better ones. We are expanding our smart and driven team and would love for you to join us.

At Dscout, we're building the human-grounded layer that teaches AI to work in the real world and proves it stays aligned there. We are expanding our smart and driven team and would love for you to join us.

Dscout AI Training & Evals builds human data and evals that show whether AI works for real people. For ten years Dscout has captured how people behave in real context, with consent and scientific rigor. Dscout AI Training & Evals points that engine at AI: consented human behavior and judgment, turned into the training data, evals, and benchmarks AI teams trust.

Models ace benchmarks and still surprise people in the wild. A benchmark says how capable a model is. It does not say whether the model works for the person using it, across weeks, in the mess of real life. That gap is where we work.

We serve AI researchers, the product builders who ship alongside them, and the research teams who partner with both. We are a new unit inside an established company: live customers, a mature platform (React, Elixir, Python, Swift, Kotlin; SOC 2 and HITRUST certified), a small senior team, and room to build. We work AI-native. Agents write code, evals gate changes, and we aim to do in months what used to take years.

A note from our Chief AI Officer & GM. The hardest AI problems show up when a model meets real people, with their tools, their interruptions, and their goals. Our customers need a partner who can design the answer, build it, and ship it fast. Ground Truth sits where deployment meets research: what we learn in the field shapes the science, and the science shapes what we ship. Come build it with us.

Why this seat

  • Work on a problem the field has not solved: measuring whether AI works for real people, over real time.
  • Study something most evals do not have: real participants, doing real tasks in their own context.
  • Own the benchmark. You are founding it, not joining a team that has one.
  • Publish. Methods and benchmarks go to the research community, with first authorship on the benchmark.
  • Join a small senior team with direct access to the Head of AI Research and the GM.

This is a research-first role focused on questions where the right rubric, benchmark, or method does not yet exist. You will find the gaps, propose bold directions, and take projects from the first hypothesis through experiments and benchmark construction to publication. You will also build: the science has to run inside live customer programs.

What you will do

Rubrics and QA science

  • Design rubrics and test whether they measure what they claim: validity, reliability, and sensitivity.
  • Measure how reliable human raters are, and when disagreement is noise versus real signal.
  • Calibrate AI judges against real human judgment, and study when they drift away from it.
  • Build quality signals that put evidence behind every data point we ship.

Long-horizon, real-user benchmarks

  • Design Dscout’s first benchmark: real users, in real context, over long horizons. Multi-week tasks across tools, not one-shot prompts.
  • Define the protocol, task design, scoring, and release. Work with our delivery team on fieldwork.
  • Work out how to keep a living benchmark honest over time: drift, contamination, difficulty, and what counts as a meaningful change.
  • Write the paper and own the public release.

Human judgment as training and eval signal

  • Study when real-world human feedback improves a model and when it adds noise.
  • Explore how preference and judgment data from representative people differ from expert data.
  • Turn findings into methods our forward deployed engineers and delivery team can run in the field.

New research directions

  • These areas are the core, not the whole list. You will have significant latitude to propose new programs, such as calibrating user simulations against real behavior, human-AI collaboration, and behavioral evaluation of agents.
  • Co-author with outside labs and academics on studies that need real-user data. Help run our paper-reading group.

A good first year

  • A QA and rubric framework running on live customer programs, with documented validity.
  • Benchmark v0 released, with a paper submitted to a top venue.
  • At least one external team using or citing our work.
  • Delivery colleagues using your methods without needing you in the room.

How we will hire: a conversation with the Head of AI Research; a research talk on your publication; a design exercise (how would you validate a rubric for a long-horizon task?); a conversation with the GM, forward deployed engineers, and delivery partners.

What we care about most. A strong publication record helps. We care most about whether you can find the question that matters, design a rigorous way to answer it, and move fast enough that the answer is still useful.

What you bring

  • Published research in evals, preference learning, reward modeling, human-AI interaction, measurement, or agent evaluation.
  • A PhD, a PhD in progress, or an MS with two or more strong research internships at labs or top industry groups. If you do not have advanced degrees but have a history of creative machine learning research work, this is just as desirable.
  • Strong applied statistics: inter-rater reliability, confidence intervals, power, and a nose for when a metric misleads.
  • Hands-on experience with LLM-as-judge, rubric-based evaluation, and preference data.
  • Strong Python, and the ability to build research prototypes and evaluation pipelines other people run. You use AI coding tools as a real part of your workflow.
  • Experience running experiments on messy human data, not only curated datasets.
  • Clear technical writing, and the ability to explain your work to a lab researcher and to a product manager.
  • Based in the Bay Area.

Nice to have: long-horizon or agentic evaluation work; psychometrics, item response theory, or human-subjects research; open-source benchmark or dataset contributions.

Compensation: $250-400K OTE + Equity. Includes a built-in bonus and equity program, publication freedom, a conference budget, flexible PTO, 15 holidays, 12 weeks of paid parental leave, 401k match, and an education stipend.

This is an ideal list. If the role excites you and you do not check every box, we would still love to hear from you.

Of course, what is outlined above is an ideal set of expectations; however, business needs and other projects and tasks may shift, and additional tasks could be assigned at the discretion of your manager.

About Dscout

Dscout is a team of passionate, empathetic, and curious professionals. As a recognized leader in the Forrester Wave, we’re at the cutting edge of experience research technology. The power of research drives us - how in-context insights from real people can build more enjoyable products and services.

We prioritize learning, sharing, and building. We also deeply value being a diverse and inclusive team and company and look for team members who align with that belief. Join our dynamic team and help shape product roadmaps and business strategies for the world’s most loved brands.

It doesn't stop there. When you join the Dscout team, you will get:

  • A strong and competitive compensation package with a built-in bonus and equity program.
  • An incredible and progressive benefits package (for both you and your dependents) to support work/life balance, including flexible PTO, 15 company holidays, 12 weeks of paid parental leave, 401k match, and much more.
  • An education stipend to support your growth & development, and a remote work stipend.
  • A company that is open and transparent with our team. You will know what is happening and why it matters.

Dscout is an equal-opportunity employer that values diversity. We do not discriminate based on identity, including race, color, religion, national origin or ancestry, sex, gender identity and expression, age, physical or mental disability, pregnancy, veteran or military status, unfavorable discharge from military service, genetic information, sexual orientation, marital status, order of protection status, citizenship status, arrest record or expunged or sealed convictions, or any other legally recognized protected basis under federal, state, or local law.

If you need reasonable accommodations for any part of the employment process, please email us at accommodations@dscout.com with the nature of your request and your contact information. We'll do everything possible to ensure you're well-prepared for success during our interview process, while also upholding your privacy, including accommodating any special requests. Please note that only inquiries regarding requests for reasonable accommodation will be responded to from this email address.

When you apply at Dscout, we will process your job applicant data, including your employment and education history, transcript, writing samples, and references, as necessary to consider your job application for open positions. For more information about our privacy practices, please visit our Privacy Policy.

Dscout participates in the E-Verify program in certain locations, as required by law.

Location Flexibility: Dscout is proud to support a remote-first workforce and enable employees to work from almost anywhere. At this time, however, we are unable to hire in the following locations: Montana, Hawaii, Alaska, and Washington DC.

NOTE: DSCOUT NEVER CONTACTS JOB APPLICANTS VIA TEXT, MESSENGER, OR OTHER SIMILAR APPLICATIONS. BE AWARE OF PHISHING AND SPOOFING SCAMS, BOTH VIA TEXT AND EMAIL. ONLY RESPOND TO EMAILS FROM DSCOUT.COM

At Life Skill Autism Academy, a division of Centria Autism, our Telehealth BCBAs lead center-based ABA therapy services virtually for children ages 12 and under.

1. Base salary up to $105,000 (based on experience).
3. Monthly and weekly bonus structure averaging $1,000 or more per month!
